thought.text: Let me examine the backend logs to understand the 503.

reasoning_content:
The backend uses issuer_url `http://auth.localhost:3000/...` to fetch JWKS. On the host, `auth.localhost` doesn't resolve (getent fails). But the backend process runs on the host and uses reqwest, which uses the system resolver. Let me check what the actual failure was in the backend log. The 503 idp_unavailable means the JWKS refresh failed or key lookup failed.

Let me check the backend logs. Where are logs? Let me find the process's log output. Also let me test whether `auth.localhost` resolution works via DNS in the container—getent said NO RESOLVE. But curl with Host header to localhost:3000 worked because we connected to localhost and set Host manually.

The backend needs `auth.localhost` to resolve to 127.0.0.1. Standard `.localhost` handling should resolve to loopback per RFC 6761, but the container's resolver isn't doing it. Let me confirm this is the cause. Let me look at the backend's log output by finding its stdout.

Let me check /proc/39011/fd.

action.command: ls -l /proc/39011/fd 2>/dev/null | head -20; echo "=== log dirs ==="; ls -la /workspace/backend/logs 2>/dev/null; find /workspace -maxdepth 3 -name "*.log" 2>/dev/null | grep -v node_modules | head; echo "=== journal ==="; ls /tmp 2>/dev/null | head -20
